items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Terminology 132:1
items.html: The vessels from the Chazeh [chest] and upward, that is, HBD HGT up to the Chazeh, are always called the inner vessels. And the reason is that the Chazeh is the aspect of the point of the conclusion of the second restriction, and therefore there is a Parsa in the middle of its body, like the Parsa beneath Atzilut, which separates between the vessels above the Chazeh, which are the aspect of Atzilut and the aspect of the inner vessels of that Partzuf, and the vessels from the Chazeh and downward, which are the aspect of BYA and the aspect of the posterior vessels of that Partzuf. Therefore all the grip of the Klipot is only in the posterior vessels, but in the inner vessels of the Partzuf they have no grip whatsoever, for even the judgments of the second restriction never struck them. (Item 143).
